title: How fast is your reflex?
hook: A falling ruler can time a blink-quick reaction. How long does a catch really take?

knows: things speed up as they fall
doesNotKnow: how to turn a fall distance into a time with d = 1/2 g t²

misconception: Reaction time is negligible, or about a second.
objective: The learner can explain that a ruler caught after a fall of about 20 cm shows a reaction time of about 0.2 s, because fall distance grows with the square of time.

claims.text: A ruler falling from rest drops a distance d = 1/2 g t² in time t, so a catch at distance d shows a reaction time t = √(2d / g).
claims.source: Constant-acceleration kinematics from rest; g = 9.81 m/s². No air drag (negligible for a ruler over 20 cm).

claims.text: A catch at 20 cm means t = √(2 × 0.20 / 9.81) = 0.20 s.
claims.source: Recomputed in node: Math.sqrt(0.4 / 9.81) = 0.2019 s (Demo.tsx timeFor).

claims.text: Typical human visual reaction time is about 0.2 to 0.25 s.
claims.source: TO CITE: a measured-reaction-time reference (for example a physiology or ruler-drop practical text). Not in the reveal text; informs the simulated catcher's mean of 0.20 s. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13: Support found: Kosinski, A Literature Review on Reaction Time (Clemson, 2008, quoting Galton and others) gives visual reaction times of 180-200 ms; Woods et al. 2015, Front. Hum. Neurosci. 9:131 report Galton's visual simple RT below 190 ms and longer, hardware-dependent values in modern samples; screen-based medians for ages 15-24 are about 220-250 ms. Suggested source text: cite Woods et al. 2015 and Kosinski 2008 instead of 'TO CITE'.

claims.text: The catcher is simulated: reaction times are drawn from a seeded random spread (seed 1) around 0.20 s, and the stage does not time the learner's own reflex.
claims.source: Demo.tsx: MEAN_T 0.20 s, SPREAD 0.05 s as the sum of three uniforms minus 1.5, SEED 1. Seed 1 was the first tried; seeds 2 and 3 give similar means (about 20 cm). Stated on stage ('Simulated catcher').

claims.text: Near a 20 cm catch, each extra centimetre of fall is about 5 thousandths of a second (so a ruler resolves hundredths of a second).
claims.source: Node: timeFor(21 cm) - timeFor(20 cm) = 0.2069 - 0.2019 = 0.0050 s.

claims.text: The learner's own catches (between the smallest and largest distances shown) convert to times on the scale by the same formula.
claims.source: Reveal computes min, max of the learner's catches from TRIALS and converts each with timeFor.

recall.question: A ruler is caught after falling 45 cm. Compared with a 20 cm catch, that reaction was...
recall.why: t = √(2 × 0.45 / 9.81) = 0.30 s, against 0.20 s for 20 cm. More fall means a longer wait, but distance grows with time squared.
